messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis of test `testIsSameLocalTime_Cal`

Details:
1. The test `testIsSameLocalTime_Cal` checks whether two `Calendar` instances represent the same local time regardless of differences in their time zones.
2. The test sets calendars `cal1` and `cal2` both to the same local time (July 9, 2004, 13:45:00) but different time zones (GMT+1 and GMT-1).
3. Similarly, `cal3` and `cal4` are set to different local times and are checked to assert they are not the same local time.
4. The failure indicates that `DateUtils.isSameLocalTime` incorrectly determined the local time equivalence.
5. The implementation of `DateUtils.isSameLocalTime` compares several Calendar fields (MILLISECOND, SECOND, MINUTE, HOUR, DAY_OF_YEAR, YEAR, ERA) and also compares the class of the Calendar objects.
6. A crucial point is the use of `Calendar.HOUR` in the comparison instead of `Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY`.
7. `Calendar.HOUR` returns the hour in 12-hour format (0–11) without AM/PM consideration, which can cause false positives when times differ by 12 hours.
8. The test with `cal3` and `cal4` sets times 4:00 and 16:00 (4 PM) respectively, which differ by 12 hours.
9. Because `Calendar.HOUR` is the same (4), the method wrongly treats these times as the same.
10. The test expects `false` in this case and fails because the method returns `true`.

The root cause of the bug is that `isSameLocalTime` compares `Calendar.HOUR` instead of `Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY`, causing it to ignore AM/PM and leading to incorrect equality results.

Suggested fix location:
- Change `cal1.get(Calendar.HOUR)` and `cal2.get(Calendar.HOUR)` to `cal1.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY)` and `cal2.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY)` in `DateUtils.isSameLocalTime(Calendar, Calendar)`.

Potentially also review the final comparison of `cal1.getClass() == cal2.getClass()`, but the primary issue is the hour field.

Methods to be fixed:
org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DateUtils.isSameLocalTime(java.util.Calendar,java.util.Calendar)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
